- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml
  Lines 5304-5340, the "Telegram review-blocked judge decision" step
  Problem: The Telegram step routes on `JUDGE_SKIP_REASON` via a `case` statement (lines 5326-5339) that has explicit branches for `disabled`, `not_writable`, `llm_failed*`, and `json_parse_failed*`, but has NO branches for the 7 new skip reasons introduced in this PR (`blocking_check_runs`, `check_runs_query_failed`, `unresolved_head_sha`, `sync_merge_failed`, `auto_merge_disabled`, `merge_conflict`, `mergeability_pending`). These all fall through to the generic `*)` branch which emits "PR review blocked — autofix exhausted (N iterations) / Needs human intervention" — the exact same misleading message this PR set out to fix on the PR comment channel.
  Why: When the judge approves a merge_with_followup but the check-runs gate refuses it, the PR comment correctly says "merge gated by in-flight check-runs" while the Telegram alert says "autofix exhausted (5 iterations)" — actively misleading operators about the real cause. ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3.
- scripts/review_rb_judge.sh
  Location: Line 1069, 1123, 1126, 1154, 1158, 1163, 1166 — all `echo "judge_skip_reason=..." >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"` lines
  Issue: Multiple `>> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"` appends for the same output name across an if/elif/else chain. While the control flow ensures only one branch executes, using `>>` (append) means a future refactor that restructures the branching could inadvertently produce duplicate output lines.
  Why: GitHub Actions takes the last value, so the blast radius is low, but it's a latent footgun. Suggested minimal fix: No change needed — the current if/elif/else structure is correct and `>>` is the standard Actions pattern. Flagging for awareness only. Estimated lines changed: 0. HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 0.
=== END FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5 ===
